newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek FRNs slip, ecu/drachma breaks 309.5.
newsitem.headline: Greek FRNs slip, ecu/drachma breaks 309.5.

text.p: Greek FRNs extended their losing streak on heavy selling by foreign players with discount margins rising to 120 basis points in late dealings from 115 at the opening, traders said.
Depos and forex forwards were fluctuating narrowly, holding morning levels with the central bank draining about 40 billion drachmas via its money market operations on Wednesday.
The drachma was steady against the ecu, having cracked the 309.50 support level around mid-session but was unable to register fresh gains in late dealings, trading around 309.42/47, dealers said.
"FRNs suffered fresh losses today with discount margins soaring to 120 basis points from 115 in the morning," said a senior bond trader at a private bank. "Market sentiment has turned bearish."
Foreign players have been net sellers of FRNs driving prices lower, the dealer said.

"High interbank money rates have hurt bonds and FRNs but other factors have played an important role," he said. "Foreign investors who have been bruised lately in some emerging markets seek to reduce exposure in Greek FRNs disregarding high discount margins."
A bond dealer at a foreign bank said foreign investors feared that they would get trapped in a situation where there would be no bids for bonds locally if a crisis erupted.
"These guys fear that they will be no exit judging from what happened in some emerging markets and rush to sell," the bond dealer said.
All dealers agreed that lower interbank rates, a smaller supply of new issues by the finance ministry and some other good news were necessary for the market to break out of its current bearish cycle.
Greece is to auction 150 billion drachmas of seven-year floaters on July 29.
Fixed coupon bonds were holding low price levels in lacklustre trading.
Depos and forex forwards held morning levels, money dealers said.

"Depos and forex forwards are holding but all eyes are on spot forex developments that affect liquidity," said a senior dealer at a foreign bank. "The central bank's move to drain a net amount of 40 billion drachmas from the system today is consistent with its policy."
The dealer estimated surplus liquidity parked at the central bank between 200 and 250 billion drachmas.
The central bank drained 40 billion drachmas of 14-day funds at 11.90 percent in its regular depo tender. A pact of 100 billion drachmas for 14-day funds matured today.
A pact of about 97 billion drachmas for 5-day repo funds also expired on Wednesday.
The mark was quoted at 156.10/20 from Wednesday's 156.080 fix, the dollar at 285.59/69 drachmas from 285.420 and the ecu at 309.43/53 from 309.41 drachmas.
